findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - Forge runs its pull-request checks and scheduled full suite.
The changed container setting conflicts with `tests/test_lanes_ci.py:44`, which still requires `ubuntu-latest`. The pinned jobs in `.github/workflows/forge.yml:49` also conflict with `tests/test_ci_limits_pull_requests_to_linux.py:82`. Finally, `src/forge/init.py:25` changes the help text, but the golden at `tests/test_split_commands.py:191`, used by `tests/test_split_commands_rest.py:48` and `tests/test_commands_load_only_their_owner.py:105`, still expects the old text. These assertions make the related CI and full-suite runs fail. Updating the help golden also changes a parametrized test ID recorded in `.test_durations:915`, which the named timing-inventory check requires to remain current.
findings.title: CI: Update tests that still expect ubuntu-latest

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - checking Forge's workflow runner pins on a pull request.
The named proof reads only `forge-next.yml` (`tests/test_rules.py:18`) and checks that the string `ubuntu-24.04` occurs somewhere, not that each Ubuntu job uses it. For example, changing the selector in `.github/workflows/starter-smoke.yml:24` back to `ubuntu-latest` leaves this proof green, and the starter test jobs can still pass on 24.04. The proof therefore does not enforce the requested pin across Forge's workflows.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_rules.py::test_31_speed

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - an earlier-adopted repository syncs its existing workflow or uses a custom runner for scheduled jobs.
The copied adopted fixture has no `.github/workflows/forge.yml`, and `tests/conftest.py:479` seeds only a README, so both adopted cases create a workflow rather than update the old `ubuntu-latest` workflow. A sync that rewrites other fields but retains the old runner would pass this proof. Also, `_jobs` and `_runner` in `tests/test_ci_runner_selection.py:34` inspect only the first runner in each slice, leaving the scheduled `full-suite` and `full-suite-result` jobs unchecked; an explicit runner applied only to pull-request jobs would pass.

findings.body:
Gain 1, Work 1, Harm 1
The `new` case repeats the same initialization and generated-job assertions already owned by `tests/test_ci_runner_selection.py:62`, using the same helpers. Retaining one boundary check avoids running the same contract twice.
